journeysCovered: information-hierarchy
competition-visibility

issues.observation: Home leads with 'WHO'S THE BITCH? · WEEK 4 OF 14', a huge '2nd', '— held', '10 points back of the lead.', 'Partial month · floors waived'. Nothing on Home or any other screen says what a point is, how a round becomes points, or how the season is won.
issues.expected: A first-time user can learn the game's basic loop from the phone in one tap.
issues.actual: No tagline, no 'how points work', no link from the rank card. The organizer would have to explain it verbally.
issues.impact: An invitee sees a rank and a gap with no way to act on either.
issues.recommendation: Add a one-line definition on first session and a tappable 'How points work' under the rank card.
issues.userAssumption: Points come from posting rounds vs my handicap; the app never confirms.

issues.observation: Home says 'WEEK 4 OF 14'; Clubhouse says 'WK 4 / 13', '13 wks' and the tile reads 'W4 / 13'.
issues.expected: One season length everywhere.
issues.actual: Two different season lengths on the two most-visited screens.
issues.impact: The most basic season fact is inconsistent; every other number loses credibility.
issues.recommendation: Single source for week count; fix whichever is wrong.

issues.observation: The Board shows only 'TODAY · AUG 29' and one line '◆ Your league is live — post the first round', plus 'Message the league...' and a dim 'Send'. Home shows Galen's 79 posted Sun Aug 23 and 'Show earlier · 18'.
issues.expected: The board carries the same activity Home summarises.
issues.actual: The screen called 'the board' says the league has no rounds while Home shows 18+ items; no league name on the board to explain which league it is.
issues.impact: The social spine looks dead to a first-time user; contradicts Home.
issues.recommendation: Show round/story items on the board, or make the empty state say what the board excludes and which league it belongs to.
issues.interpretation: Either a load-timing artefact (9 s), a different league, or the board only shows chat — none is explained on screen.

issues.observation: Standings: '01 Galen (LOCKED) 19' then a sub-line '10 back of Galen' then a divider, then '02 You · Jerech... (LOCKED) 9'. The gap line is drawn under Galen's row.
issues.expected: The gap sentence belongs to my row.
issues.actual: It reads as if Galen is 10 back of himself.
issues.impact: The one sentence that tells me my deficit is attached to the wrong golfer.
issues.recommendation: Render the gap line inside the viewer's row.

issues.observation: 'tee sheet' appears five times ('ON THE TEE SHEET' label, legend, 'Tap any day to put a round on the tee sheet.', CTA 'Put a round on the tee sheet', section 'ON THE TEE SHEET') and is never defined.
issues.expected: The primary CTA uses a word a first-timer understands.
issues.actual: Jargon in the primary action.
issues.recommendation: Say 'Plan a round' / 'Rounds you've planned' and define tee sheet once if the term stays.
issues.userAssumption: tee sheet = scheduled rounds

issues.observation: The live screen opens with caps 'SET UP THE ROUND' and no nav title, no back/close, no game name. Copy: 'Pick who plays with who under the game — pairings, stakes, the lot.'
issues.expected: The screen says what it starts (live scoring? match play? a bet?) and how to leave.
issues.actual: Neither the purpose nor the exit is visible; 'the game' is never named.
issues.recommendation: Title the screen with the game/format and add a visible Close; state what happens on start.

issues.observation: Score boxes show '41' and '43' in grey under 'FRONT 9 GROSS' / 'BACK 9 GROSS' while 'GROSS —' and the preview bar are empty.
issues.expected: Empty inputs look empty.
issues.actual: Placeholders read as entered values at phone glance; a first-timer may think the app already has a score or post without noticing the boxes are blank.
issues.recommendation: Use '—' or 'e.g. 41' placeholders, or none.
issues.userAssumption: 41/43 were values the app already knew.

issues.observation: Preview card copy: 'Enter at least one nine.' and 'A preview at 100% of your number — your league's own math scores it on the books.'
issues.expected: Plain language: what the preview shows and why it may differ from the league score.
issues.actual: '100% of your number', 'your league's own math', 'on the books' are undefined.
issues.recommendation: 'This estimate uses your full handicap; your league's rules may score it differently.'

issues.observation: The AUG 2026 grid has an empty first row and its second row starts at 6 (T F S). Aug 1 2026 is a Saturday; days 1–5 are absent while past days 6–8 are drawn dim.
issues.expected: Every day of the month renders.
issues.actual: Five days missing; looks broken.
issues.recommendation: Render 1–5 (dimmed if past).

issues.observation: The You card's top-left caps label reads 'NO. 2'. On Settings the selected ball-marker tile is named 'No. 2'. The user is simultaneously in 2nd place on Home.
issues.expected: A label that cannot be mistaken for rank.
issues.actual: The marker's name collides with the user's actual rank; reads as standing.
issues.recommendation: Drop the marker name from the card header or prefix it ('Marker · No. 2').
issues.userAssumption: NO. 2 = my rank.

issues.observation: Pills and lines 'LOCKED' (both standings rows), '— held', 'Partial month · floors waived', 'no floor to clear' are shown with no definition.
issues.expected: Status words are self-explanatory or tappable.
issues.actual: Four undefined status terms on the two primary screens.
issues.recommendation: Replace with plain phrases ('no change', 'no minimum this month') or add a tap-to-explain.

issues.observation: Home says '2nd' and '10 points back of the lead.' The leader is not named and the field size is not shown; Clubhouse reveals only two golfers.
issues.expected: Home tells me who I'm chasing and out of how many.
issues.actual: '2nd' of an unstated 2 reads as a podium when it is last place.
issues.recommendation: '2nd of 2 · 10 back of Galen' on the rank card.

issues.observation: Section 'THIS WEEK' contains a card dated 'Sun, Aug 23' on Sat Aug 29 (Clubhouse: 'Week closes Sun', season started Mon Aug 3, so Aug 23 closed week 3). 'QUIET SINCE YOUR LAST VISIT' is immediately followed by an item.
issues.expected: Section labels match their contents.
issues.actual: Last week's round under 'This week'; 'quiet' headline over a non-empty list.
issues.recommendation: Use 'Latest' / 'Recent' or align the window with the league week; reword the quiet line.

issues.observation: Crew row: 'Galen BUDDY · FRI SEP 4 · QUINTERO GOLF AND COUNTRY CLUB · you lead 1–0 · YOU'RE IN · "Major" · ON THE TEE SHEET'.
issues.expected: Each token is understandable.
issues.actual: 'you lead 1–0' (in what?), 'YOU'RE IN' (in what?), '"Major"' (a nickname? format?) are unexplained.
issues.recommendation: 'Head-to-head vs Galen: 1–0', 'You're confirmed', and label the round's nickname.

issues.observation: Legend '● SEASON DATE'; blue dots sit on Sundays 9, 16, 23, 30 with no explanation of why Sundays are season dates.
issues.expected: Calendar markers explain what they mean.
issues.actual: A rule (weekly Sunday deadline?) is implied by dots only.
issues.recommendation: 'Week closes' or 'Season week ends' instead of 'Season date'.

issues.observation: Header card: 'POINTS RACE · STANDARD RULES', 'THE PRO · GALEN', pill 'Code · WHOS84L9', link 'Add golfers' during a live season.
issues.expected: Format, ruleset, organizer role and code purpose are each explained or tappable.
issues.actual: Three undefined terms plus a code with no instruction.
issues.recommendation: 'Format: points race (see rules)', 'Organizer: Galen', 'Invite code — share to join'.

issues.observation: Tile 'COUNTING ROUNDS 1 / 4 · August · your best 4 count' and footer 'EVERYONE ADVANCES — 2 CONTENDERS, 2 SEATS' imply rules (best-4 cap, an end-of-season stage) that are stated nowhere.
issues.expected: The rule is readable where it's referenced.
issues.actual: Advance to what? Seats where? Never said.
issues.recommendation: Link each to a rules sheet; name the endgame ('everyone makes the final').

issues.observation: Standings are below a nav title, a header card (league name repeated), a tab strip, four stat tiles, an August progress bar and a 'NEXT UP' card; the user's own name is truncated 'You · Jerech...' beside a LOCKED badge.
issues.expected: Standings are the first thing seen on the league screen.
issues.actual: The only who-beats-whom view on the phone is a full scroll down.
issues.recommendation: Move standings above the tiles; collapse the header card.

issues.observation: A full-width 'Find a golfer' button sits directly above a search field 'Find golfers by name or @handle'; each of six rows carries a green 'BUDDIES' pill under a 'BUDDIES · 6' header; 'REQUESTED' section gives no direction and no accept/decline control.
issues.expected: One find control; pills only where they add information; pending requests actionable.
issues.actual: Redundant controls and pills; ambiguous requests.
issues.recommendation: Single search; drop the per-row pill; label 'They asked you' vs 'You asked' with actions.

issues.observation: 'BALL MARKER' grid of 14 tiles named after famous holes (The Saguaro, The Island, The Lighthouse, The Lone Tree, The Pews, The Dunes, The Beverage, The Shark, The Azalea, The Jug, The Wee Bridge, No. 2, The Postage Stamp, The Thistle) is the largest element; caption 'YOUR PHOTO · THE MARKER ALWAYS BACKS IT UP'.
issues.expected: The purpose of the marker is stated in one line.
issues.actual: Neither purpose nor names are explained; 'backs it up' is cryptic.
issues.recommendation: 'Your marker is your icon when there's no photo' and a hint on the hole names.

issues.observation: Sheet 'Start an event · SHORT FORM · ITS OWN LITTLE TROPHY'; 'The Ryder — Two teams · weekly vs-index duels · first to the clinch — LIVE'; 'Bracket — Knockout · seeded · last golfer standing — SOON'; 'Every event mints a trophy for your display case. More styles land after the pilot.'
issues.expected: Plain-language blurbs; status words that aren't ambiguous.
issues.actual: 'vs-index duels', 'the clinch', 'mints', 'the pilot' are jargon; 'LIVE' could mean available or currently running.
issues.recommendation: 'Available' / 'Coming soon'; one plain sentence per format; remove 'pilot'.

issues.observation: 'Name your league · THE BANNER EVERYTHING HANGS UNDER', one field, 'You can rename it any time before the bylaws lock.', 'Start the league', 'Cancel'; ~80% of the screen empty; no step indicator.
issues.expected: The user knows what a league involves and how many steps remain before committing.
issues.actual: 'Start the league' from a name alone; 'bylaws lock' undefined.

explanation30s: It's a golf app where your friend group runs a season — ours is 13 or 14 weeks, the app can't decide. You post your rounds with your handicap, and somehow that turns into points; I'm in 2nd with 9, Galen has 19, and I honestly can't tell you how he got there or how I get more. There's a calendar for planning rounds together — it calls them a 'tee sheet' — and a live-scoring thing where you set up a foursome, but it never says what game you're playing. You collect badges like 'Broke 90' on your profile and pick a little icon named after a famous golf hole. There's a pot, but ours is 'bragging rights'. The organizer will have to explain the rules to you, because the app doesn't.

personaVerdict.question: As a first-time user looking only at the iPhone app's screens, do they say what Cup Season is and why I should care?
personaVerdict.answer: They say it is competitive (a rank, a gap, a leader), social (buddies, a board, a calendar) and golf-serious (index, rating/slope, gross), and the design is confident and attractive. They do not say what the game is, how a round becomes points, how a season ends, or what half the words mean. Who is beating whom is answered on exactly one screen (Clubhouse standings), below the fold, with the gap line on the wrong row. A friend would need the organizer to walk them through it.

explanation30s: Cup Season is an app where a group of golf buddies runs a season — ours is 17 weeks, September 5th to January 2nd. Everyone puts $50 in a pot, you get split into two squads by a blind draw, and every round you play anywhere counts: you post your gross score and tees, and the app scores it against your own handicap, so a 15 beating his number gets the same points as a 6 beating hers. Your best four rounds a month count for your squad, you owe at least two rounds a month, and the last four weeks are a 'Cup Final' that's scored fresh. The winning squad takes 60% of the pot, second 25%, and the top individual 15%. The catch is the app doesn't move money — Casey keeps a tab, and I still don't know how I'm supposed to pay him.

personaVerdict.question: Can you understand what you are joining before accepting?
personaVerdict.answer: No. Before the '$50' button I knew the league's name, the buy-in, 'PRESET Standard' (undefined), '2 rounds / mo' and 'Cup Final · final 4 weeks'. I did not know who was in it (not even that Casey ran it), when it started or ended, how a round scored, or how money moved. Every answer exists in the app — but only after joining, across Clubhouse tabs and a collapsed 'LEAGUE RULES & PRO SHOP' disclosure. The consent sheet is the right idea with the wrong contents, and the landing line 'Enter your email and you're in' promises the opposite of what happens. After joining, the Home screen handed me the organizer's lock/discard wizard and my first posted round earned points that then did not exist anywhere.

explanation30s: It's an app that turns our regular rounds into a season. You join Casey's league, and every time you play — anywhere — you type in your front and back nine and it scores you against your own handicap: 5 points for just posting, up to 12 if you beat your number by three. Your best four rounds a month count for your team — it splits us into two random squads — and if you don't post at least two rounds a month your team loses points. There's a fifty-dollar buy-in it keeps a tab on but doesn't actually collect, and after four months there's a final few weeks that decides who takes the pot. It also has a chat and a scorecard for side bets. Honestly the scoring idea is good; the app just doesn't tell you any of that until you dig.

personaVerdict.question: Does Cup Season provide enough obvious value to justify changing behavior?
personaVerdict.answer: Not as presented. The value that would justify switching — a fair, automatic, season-long race against your own number that a spreadsheet can't do, from any course, with a pot ledger and a final — is real but is the LEAST visible thing in the product. What's visible on day one (a chat, a calendar, a pot ledger, gross scores, a $50 ask, a Pro's lock button on my Home) is what we already have or don't want. I'd stay in the group text and let Casey run it; I'd post rounds only because he nags. If it visibly ran the race for us, $79/year split six ways would be fine.

explanation30s: It's an app for our golf group. Casey set up a 'league' for the fall — four months. Everybody chips in fifty bucks into a pot the app keeps track of, but you still pay Casey directly. It splits us into two squads by random draw. Every time you play, you type in your front and back nine and the app turns it into points — five to twelve — based on how you did against your own handicap, which it works out for you after three rounds, so a 97 from me can beat an 84 from Priya. Your best four rounds a month count for your squad, and if you don't post at least two a month your squad loses points. There's also a live scorecard thing where you can play match play or skins for five bucks while you're out there, and it posts the scores for you. At the end there's some kind of Cup Final and the pot gets split. I still don't totally get how the squad points and the individual points fit together, and I'm not sure my rounds this week even count.

personaVerdict.question: Can a normal golfer understand this without becoming a golf-league nerd?
personaVerdict.answer: Halfway. Posting a score is genuinely easy once you find the ⊕ and don't touch the Rating/Slope boxes. Understanding what the score did is not: the same round was called -9.8, 9.8 over, and +0.0 played-to-it; 5 points were promised and then not awarded with no sentence saying the season starts Sep 5. The vocabulary (the Pro, squad, pot sheet, bylaws, floor, counting cap, differential, scored fresh, Points King, SI, net best ball, Sunningdale) is never defined where you meet it, the biggest button on my Home is the organizer's job, and someone else posted a 103 to my record. I'd need Casey to explain half of it in the parking lot.

explanation30s: Cup Season is a season-long golf league app for your friend group. Everyone posts their real rounds from wherever they play, and each round scores 5 to 12 points based on how you did against your own handicap — beat your number by three and you get 12, a bad day still gets 5, so the only way to hurt your team is not to play. Your best four rounds a month count for your squad, you owe at least two a month, and there's a $50 buy-in that pays the winning squad, the runner-up and the top individual points scorer. The last four weeks are a 'Cup Final' that's scored fresh — I honestly don't know what that means yet. On the course you can run skins, match play, Wolf or Sunningdale live in the app and it settles the money hole by hole.

personaVerdict.question: Does Cup Season feel strategically compelling enough to care about all season?
personaVerdict.answer: Not yet. The live side games (skins/match/Wolf with real strokes and a netted settlement card) and the receipts that show the differential math are genuinely good and I'd use them every Saturday. The season layer is a participation contest whose rules I can't fully find — the Cup Final is one bylaw row ('Final 4 weeks · scored fresh'), ties don't exist, the 95% allowance never appears in a calculation — and it showed me zero for three posted rounds without saying why. It never gives me a rival, a gap to the leader, or a 'this round matters because' line; the only rivalry in my league today is the pride stake I typed myself. As a 6.4 I also have no reason to believe the flat 12/9/7/6/5 bands aren't tilted toward high-variance 20-handicaps. Fix the endgame explanation, the pre-season honesty and a head-to-head view and I'd care; as shipped I'd play for the skins and shrug at the table.
